answer: Each epoch the protocol snapshots J0, agents_joined at open, and a first-seen key burns B+1 units of this epoch's per-head payout, where B is joins already included since J0, struck at close. A lone joiner facing B=0 burns 1. A farm that already parked nine new keys burns 10, so the next head costs more than the last. B is network-global: a fresh key cannot reset, split, or pre-age it, because agents_joined only rises. Refuse the burn and the submit is dropped. New keys enter the garden only through that juniper meter; the meadow records B.
